seoTitle: How to Archive Workspace Email Instead of Deleting a User
metaDescription: Learn how to archive a Google Workspace user's email instead of deleting the account, preserving data for compliance while saving on billing.
intro: When an employee leaves, the instinct is to delete their account and stop paying for the seat right away. The problem is that deleting a Google Workspace user can also delete their mailbox and Drive files, which is a real risk if you ever need that data for legal, financial, or reference purposes. Google Workspace has a built-in alternative: archive the account instead of deleting it. Archiving blocks sign-in and frees the account's active license immediately, while keeping the mailbox and files intact for an admin to search or export later. It isn't free on every plan, and the button you need is filed in a different place depending on your edition, both of which this guide covers alongside the retention and file-ownership steps that come before and after it.
prerequisites: An administrator account on Business Starter, Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus, or an Education edition — archiving isn't available on every Workspace plan
An Archived User subscription already on your billing account, or be ready to buy one when prompted (Flexible Plan customers are billed automatically per archived account instead)
costNote: Archiving isn't free on Business or Enterprise plans. It requires an Archived User subscription, purchased separately through Billing > Subscriptions or billed automatically per account on the Flexible Plan. It costs less than an active license, but Google doesn't publish a fixed rate; check your own Billing > Subscriptions screen for the actual figure. Education editions include Archived User licenses at no extra charge.

steps.heading: Open the Admin console
steps.body: Sign in to admin.google.com with an administrator account. Google requires an admin-level login for this, not a regular user's own sign-in, because archiving changes something that affects your organization's billing. The Admin console home shows a Manage Workspace panel with Users and Billing side by side, a reminder that every active seat is billed and that archiving a user is really a billing change dressed up as a user-management one.

image.caption: The Admin console home, with Users and Billing panels next to each other under Manage Workspace.

steps.heading: Go to Directory and open Users
steps.body: From the left-hand menu, expand Directory and click Users to see every account in your organization, along with each person's status, last sign-in, and email usage. Find the departing employee's row and confirm the address matches the account you mean to change before doing anything else. A wrong click here reaches a real mailbox.

image.caption: The Users list in Directory, showing each account's status, last sign-in time, and email storage usage.

steps.heading: Select the user and archive the account
steps.body: Check the box next to the person's name so the toolbar shows "1 user selected," then click More options. What happens next depends on your edition. On Enterprise Standard, Enterprise Plus, and Education plans, More options lists Archive user directly. On Business Starter, Standard, and Plus, select Delete user first: Google's dialog surfaces an Archive user button inside that flow instead of listing it as its own menu entry, and if your organization has no Archived User subscription yet you'll be prompted to buy one there. Either path ends the same way: the account is blocked from signing in and stops receiving new mail immediately, its mailbox and Drive files stay in place, and its original license is freed for reassignment. This is a different action from Suspend, which also blocks sign-in but leaves the full-price license attached to the account.

image.caption: A single user selected in the Users list, with the More options menu open to reveal offboarding actions like suspending the account.

steps.heading: Set a Vault retention hold if you need one
steps.body: If your organization must keep the mailbox for a set period, apply a retention rule in Google Vault before archiving, so the mail stays searchable independent of whatever else happens to the license. How long to keep it depends on your industry and location, so check with whoever handles compliance if you're unsure. Vault is a separate add-on; archiving on its own does not create a retention hold.

steps.heading: Transfer ownership of shared Drive files
steps.body: Check what Drive files the departing user owned and reassign anything the team still needs to an active teammate. An archived account still holds its files, but leaving ownership as it is means only an admin can reach them afterward, which orphans a live project the moment someone else needs to edit it. This step is easy to skip in the moment and usually the one that causes problems weeks later.

troubleshooting.problem: More options has no Archive user entry
troubleshooting.cause: On Business Starter, Standard, and Plus, Archive user isn't a separate menu item. It's inside the Delete user dialog, or your edition doesn't support archiving at all.
troubleshooting.fix: Click Delete user and look for an Archive user button before confirming. If it isn't there, check that your plan is Business Starter/Standard/Plus, Enterprise Standard/Plus, or an Education edition.

troubleshooting.problem: The console prompts you to buy an Archived User subscription
troubleshooting.cause: No Archived User subscription exists yet on the billing account, and Business and Enterprise plans require one before you can archive anyone.
troubleshooting.fix: Buy the subscription when prompted, or check Billing > Subscriptions first if you're not sure one already exists. Flexible Plan accounts skip this step and are billed automatically per archived user.

troubleshooting.problem: A shared file goes missing from a live project after archiving
troubleshooting.cause: Ownership of that file was never transferred, and only an admin can reach an archived account's Drive data now.
troubleshooting.fix: Transfer ownership to an active teammate before you archive, or have a super admin do it afterward from the archived account's Drive files.

faq.question: What's the difference between suspending and archiving a user?
faq.answer: Suspend blocks sign-in immediately but leaves the account on its full-price license, still billed as active. Archive also blocks sign-in, but swaps the account onto a separate Archived User license and frees the original one for reassignment. Suspending is instant and reversible with one click; archiving is the step that changes what you're billed for a departing employee.

faq.question: Does archiving a user cost anything?
faq.answer: On Business and Enterprise plans, yes — it needs an Archived User subscription, bought separately or billed automatically per account on the Flexible Plan. It costs less than an active license, though Google doesn't publish a fixed price; your Billing > Subscriptions screen shows the actual rate for your account. On Education plans, Archived User licenses are included at no extra charge.

faq.question: On Business plans, doesn't clicking Delete user delete the account?
faq.answer: No. On Business Starter, Standard, and Plus, Delete user is the dialog that contains the Archive user button, not a separate deletion. Choose Archive, not the delete option, and the account is archived, not removed.

faq.question: Do I need Google Vault to preserve an archived user's email?
faq.answer: Vault makes retention and legal hold easier to apply and search, but archiving itself already blocks sign-in and keeps the mailbox intact for an admin. Add Vault when you have a specific retention period to enforce, not as a requirement for archiving to work.

faq.question: What happens to Drive files owned by an archived user?
faq.answer: They stay attached to the account and remain accessible to admins, but nobody else can reach or edit them unless you transfer ownership first. Do that before you archive, for any file the team still needs.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in August 2026. The suspend-versus-archive distinction, the edition-dependent More options flow, the Archived User subscription requirement, and the Vault/retention behaviour were re-checked in September 2026 against Google's own Admin Help pages on archiving former employees and adding Archived User licenses. That check corrected this guide's earlier framing of archiving as simply "suspend, then relicense."
